official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year, Cohort 5 (undergraduate track). The programme's own portal states the postgraduate track for the same 2026/2027 intake is closed (it ran 23 Jul to 25 Aug 2026).
official.status_note: The recruitment portal states 'Undergraduate Scholarships are open' for 2026/2027 Cohort 5, with applications closing 12 Oct 2026, 23:59 Kigali time; the 2026/2027 postgraduate track is marked Closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Comprehensive financial support, including full tuition fees, fully paid on-campus accommodation, a laptop, learning materials, an annual return ticket allowance, and a full-year monthly stipend.' The programme FAQ adds: 'Financial support includes, but not limited to, tuition fees, registration fees, accommodation, learning tools and materials including laptop and other scholastic materials, return ticket to a Mastercard Foundation Scholar's Country of origin, if necessary, among others.'
benefits: Comprehensive financial support, including full tuition fees, fully paid on-campus accommodation, a laptop, learning materials, an annual return ticket allowance, and a full-year monthly stipend
Uniquely sourced internships with industry partners for professional development
Continued academic support through academic mentorship, virtual learning, and tutoring
Career development services, including industrial mentorship, career guidance, and professional development

Regular group meetings with other scholars, opportunities to participate in leadership congresses, community service, and mentoring through the 'Go Back, Give Back' initiative, and the prestige of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Alumni network
eligibility: Be a citizen of Rwanda or any African country, a refugee, or a displaced young person in Africa
Demonstrate critical social and/or economic needs and/or disability

For undergraduate applicants, be not older than 28 years at the time of application, or not older than 30 years for those with certified proof of a protracted life condition (e.g., refugees, single mothers, members of child-headed families, etc.)
Meet the admission criteria for eligible programs at the University of Rwanda
Have proven records of leadership and community engagement
Show a strong commitment to community engagement and be prepared to 'Go Back' and/or 'Give Back' to their community
Refugees and individuals with disabilities are expected to provide legal proof of their status
Applicants must be newly admitted students who have not yet started their studies at the University of Rwanda
requirements: Apply for admission to a first-year undergraduate program at the University of Rwanda for the 2026/2027 academic year - this is mandatory before applying for the scholarship
Meet the admission criteria for one of the eligible programs listed by the programme
Applicants with foreign academic qualifications must obtain an equivalence from Rwanda's Higher Education Council (HEC) and the National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA)
Refugees and individuals with disabilities must provide legal proof of their status
Complete the online application in the recruitment portal and submit before 12 Oct 2026, 23:59 (Kigali time)
Include your full name and application number in any correspondence to the programme
documents: Your University of Rwanda student number (9-digit UR registration number, issued after applying for admission) - all applicants
Digital passport photo, white background - all applicants
Scanned National ID showing date of birth, passport or refugee ID - all applicants
Leadership certificates - if you have any
Legal proof of refugee status or disability - refugees and individuals with disabilities
selection_criteria: Applications are assessed using a standard weighting scale: Academic Talent 30%, Economic Disadvantage 45%, Leadership Potential 25%
The selection process includes application review, shortlisting, interviews, and verification of financial need
Final selection is based on merit and alignment with the program's values and criteria
Academic excellence, strong leadership potential, commitment to community service, resilience, and a clear vision for contributing to Africa's transformation
coverage: Full tuition fees and registration fees
A laptop and learning tools and materials, including other scholastic materials
A full-year monthly stipend (the programme publishes no cash figure for it)
An annual return ticket allowance; the FAQ describes a return ticket to the scholar's country of origin, if necessary
Psycho-social support services, academic mentorship, virtual learning and tutoring, career development services, and internships
application_method: Verify and create an account: enter your University of Rwanda student number to confirm you are eligible, then create your account
Complete the form: fill in your identification, education background, family, socio-economic and leadership information across six short sections (A to E)
Review your answers, submit, and track your application status from your dashboard at any time
Continue an existing application or track application status and results through the same portal
Contact the programme at mcfsp@ur.ac.rw with your full name and application number
official.application_route: First lodge a University of Rwanda first-year admission application for 2026/2027 and obtain your 9-digit UR student number, then apply online at mcfsprecruitment.ur.ac.rw/ug-recruitment.
official.study_mode: full-time (eligible programmes are published as 'FULL TIME DAY')
official.citizenship_residency: Be a citizen of Rwanda or any African country, a refugee, or a displaced young person in Africa.
official.international_eligibility: Open to African nationals, refugees and displaced youth in Africa. The portal states an entry visa is granted on arrival at Kigali International Airport to citizens of all countries, and that international students must apply for a study visa within 15 days of arrival with a police clearance and a valid passport. The programme's published targets reserve 15% of places for international students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to programs on the programme's published MCFSP Eligible Programs list (35 undergraduate qualifications across the Colleges of Agriculture/Forestry/Food Science, Arts and Social Sciences, Business and Economics, Education, Medicine and Health Sciences, Science and Technology, and Veterinary Medicine and Animal Sciences, at the Busogo, Huye, Rukara, Nyarugenge and Nyagatare campuses), and the applicant must first be admitted to a first-year undergraduate program at the University of Rwanda for 2026/2027.
official.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda is a 10-year partnership (2021-2031) between the University of Rwanda and the Mastercard Foundation that aims to develop the next generation of transformative leaders by enabling highly talented, service-oriented young people, primarily young Africans, to pursue higher education and cultivate their leadership potential. It awards full scholarships to talented young people from economically disadvantaged backgrounds for a bachelor's degree at the University of Rwanda, with priority focus on young women, refugees and displaced persons, and persons with disabilities.
official.program_type: University undergraduate scholarship (first-year bachelor's degree at the University of Rwanda)

applicant_utility.summary: This is the undergraduate track of the University of Rwanda's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for the 2026/2027 Cohort 5 intake, and the portal was still showing an open countdown to 12 October 2026, 23:59 Kigali time on 11 October 2026 - so there is essentially one day left in this cycle. You cannot even begin the form until you hold a 9-digit UR student number, which means a University of Rwanda first-year admission application for 2026/2027 must already have been lodged and processed. The published award covers full tuition, registration fees, fully paid on-campus accommodation, a laptop, learning materials, an annual return ticket allowance and a full-year monthly stipend, but the programme never states a cash figure for the stipend, so budget from the coverage list rather than a quoted amount and confirm the value directly with the programme office.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically credible first-year UR applicants from economically disadvantaged households, especially young women, refugees or displaced youth, and applicants with disabilities who can document both hardship and community leadership.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for University of Rwanda first-year admission for 2026/2027 and obtain your 9-digit student number before touching the scholarship portal - the portal blocks entry without it
Draft the socio-economic section first and keep evidence for every claim; it carries 45% of the total weight, more than academic talent
Collect leadership certificates and any community-service records before opening the form; they feed the 25% leadership weighting
Prepare scans at moderate resolution as PDF/JPG/PNG under 5 MB each so uploads do not stall near the deadline
If your secondary qualification is from outside Rwanda, start the HEC and NESA equivalence process now rather than after submitting
Email mcfsp@UR.ac.rw with your full name and application number for any query, as the programme instructs
common_rejection_risks: A strong transcript paired with thin financial-need evidence loses here: economic disadvantage is weighted 45% against 30% for academic talent
Applying after having already started your UR studies - the programme explicitly refuses applicants who are already enrolled

Being over 28 at the time of application, since the 30-year allowance only applies with certified proof of a protracted life condition such as refugee status, single motherhood or membership of a child-headed family
Submitting the scholarship application before the UR admission application has been processed, leaving no student number to verify against
Claims in the socio-economic section that cannot be verified during the financial-need verification step
Applying for a programme that is not on the published MCFSP Eligible Programs list, or for a place your foreign qualification has not been equated for
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The programme publishes no cash figure for the stipend, so the applicant should assume personal transport and communications, clothing and personal items, any family support obligations beyond the stated allowance, and - for non-Rwandans - the student visa, police clearance and the HEC/NESA equivalence process. Ask mcfsp@UR.ac.rw for the actual stipend and accommodation terms before committing family funds.
document_audit: The student number is a gate rather than an attachment: the portal will not advance past step 1 without a valid 9-digit UR registration number issued after applying for admission
National ID, passport or refugee ID scans must visibly show the date of birth; cropped or expired images are the most avoidable upload failure
The passport photo must be a digital image on a white background - a phone photo taken against a wall will fail on quality
Disability certificates and leadership certificates are conditional uploads: supply them only where they apply, but do supply genuine leadership certificates
Refugees and applicants with disabilities must hold legal proof of status before applying, because the programme expects it at application rather than later
Foreign-qualified applicants need the HEC/NESA equivalence in hand; without it the academic-merit component cannot be assessed
alerts: Timing trap: on 11 October 2026 the undergraduate portal was still counting down to 12 October 2026, 23:59 Kigali time - the cycle is effectively at its end, so treat this year as all but lost and prepare for the next call rather than starting a fresh application now
The 2026/2027 postgraduate track is already closed (it ran 23 July to 25 August 2026), so master's applicants should monitor the announcements page instead of waiting for this portal to reopen
You must already hold a UR student number; without a processed UR admission application you are locked out at verification and no exception is published
The award is renewable annually only subject to satisfactory academic performance, discipline and continued financial need, so the benefit is conditional rather than guaranteed for four years
Non-Rwandan holders must apply for a study visa within 15 days of arrival with a police clearance and a valid passport, so budget and plan documents before travelling

Each intake is competitive against published quotas: 70% women, 25% refugees, 10% persons with disabilities, 80% STEM, so a non-STEM, male, non-refugee profile competes for the smallest share of places
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One-stage online submission at the UR recruitment portal: verify your student number, create an account, complete sections A-E, review and submit before 23:59 Kigali time on 12 October 2026, then monitor the same portal's track dashboard for status and results.
